config.title: useDebounce

intro.title: useDebounce
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a search input component that delays sending requests until the user stops typing, preventing too many rapid calls. You will learn the core concept of debouncing, which controls how often a function runs by waiting for a pause in activity. The main technologies involved are Angular's reactive forms, RxJS operators like debounceTime, and TypeScript for type safety. By the end, you'll create a functional search bar that efficiently handles user input.
intro.usecase: Debouncing is essential in Angular applications where user interactions trigger frequent updates that could overwhelm APIs or cause performance issues. In real-world dashboards, debouncing prevents excessive API calls when users adjust filters or search inputs, ensuring smooth data loading. Form validation benefits from debouncing by delaying checks until users pause typing, improving responsiveness. This pattern also enhances autocomplete suggestions and live search features in e-commerce platforms by reducing server load while maintaining a responsive user experience.

objectives: Construct a custom Angular directive that implements debounce logic.
Initialize and manage a timer using RxJS operators within the directive.
Bind the directive to an input element to control event emission.
Configure the debounce duration via an input property.
Update the directive to emit a debounced value to a parent component.
Integrate the debounce directive into a component template to manipulate user input flow.

steps.instruction: Create a component class named DebounceDemoComponent that implements the OnInit interface.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator above the class and include the OnInit interface in the implements clause.

steps.title: Add search input state property
steps.instruction: Inside the DebounceDemoComponent class, add a public property named 'searchTerm' of type string with an initial empty value.
steps.hint: Declare the property in the class body, not inside a method. Use TypeScript type annotation.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a reactive property to store the search input value.
successCriteria: The DebounceDemoComponent class contains a 'searchTerm' property of type string initialized to an empty string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've declared a property named 'searchTerm' with type 'string' and initialized it to an empty string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The property is missing or incorrect. Add 'searchTerm: string = "";' inside the DebounceDemoComponent class.

steps.title: Add debounced search result state property
steps.instruction: In the DebounceDemoComponent class, add a property named debouncedResult of type string with an initial empty value.
steps.hint: Add a new property declaration in the class body, similar to how you added the searchInput property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a debouncedResult property to store the debounced search result.
successCriteria: The DebounceDemoComponent class contains a debouncedResult property of type string initialized to an empty string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a property, but check that it's named exactly 'debouncedResult' and has type 'string' with an initial empty value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The debouncedResult property is missing or incorrect. Add 'debouncedResult: string = "";' inside the class.

steps.title: Define the debounce handler method
steps.instruction: Inside the DebounceDemoComponent class, define a private method named debounce that takes a callback function and delay time as parameters, and returns a debounced version of the callback.
steps.hint: The method should have two parameters: a callback function and a delay number. Inside, use setTimeout to delay execution and clearTimeout to cancel previous calls.
steps.expectedOutcome: A private debounce method is added to the component class with proper TypeScript typing for parameters and return type.
successCriteria: The component contains a private method named debounce that accepts a callback function and delay number, and returns a function that implements debounce logic.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but check: Is it named 'debounce'? Does it take callback and delay parameters? Does it return a debounced function?
steps.feedbackWrong: The debounce method is missing or incorrect. Review the method signature and implementation: it should be private, take two parameters, and return a function that uses setTimeout and clearTimeout.

steps.title: Create the search handler with debounce
steps.instruction: Inside the DebounceDemoComponent class, create a method called onSearchInput that updates the debouncedResult property after a 500ms delay using the debounce handler method you defined earlier.
steps.hint: Call your debounce handler method inside onSearchInput and pass it a function that updates debouncedResult with the current searchInput value.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an onSearchInput method that uses the debounceHandler to update debouncedResult after 500ms when called.
successCriteria: The onSearchInput method exists, calls debounceHandler with a function that updates debouncedResult, and specifies a 500ms delay.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your onSearchInput method calls debounceHandler and updates debouncedResult with the current searchInput value after 500ms.
steps.feedbackWrong: The onSearchInput method is missing or doesn't properly use the debounce handler to update debouncedResult after 500ms.

steps.title: Initialize debounced search in ngOnInit
steps.instruction: Inside the ngOnInit method, call the onSearchInput method with the initial searchInput value to trigger the debounced search when the component loads.
steps.hint: You can call onSearchInput() directly in ngOnInit. Since onSearchInput expects an event parameter, you can pass a mock event object or call it without arguments if you adjust the method to handle the initial call.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ngOnInit method will now initialize the debounced search behavior by calling onSearchInput when the component first loads.
successCriteria: ngOnInit contains a call to onSearchInput.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you call onSearchInput inside ngOnInit.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the instruction: you need to call onSearchInput inside the ngOnInit method.

steps.title: Add the component template with search input
steps.instruction: Add a template to the component decorator that includes an input field bound to the searchInput property using ngModel.
steps.hint: Use the ngModel directive with two-way binding syntax [(ngModel)] and add a placeholder attribute to the input.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a template with an input field that is bound to the searchInput property.
successCriteria: The template includes an input element with [(ngModel)] binding to searchInput and a placeholder attribute.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added the input field, but make sure to use [(ngModel)] for two-way binding and include a placeholder.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template is missing or incorrect. Add an input element with [(ngModel)]="searchInput" and a placeholder.

steps.title: Wire input event to search handler
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add an (input) event binding to the search input element that calls the onSearchInput() method when the user types.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax: (input)="onSearchInput()". This connects the input event to your search handler.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: wiring an input event
<input (input)="handleInput()" placeholder="Type here">
steps.expectedOutcome: The search input element will trigger the onSearchInput() method whenever the user types, enabling the debounced search functionality.
successCriteria: The template contains an input element with an (input) event binding that calls onSearchInput().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the (input) event binding to call onSearchInput() on the input element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input event isn't properly connected to the search handler. Check that you're using Angular's (input) event binding syntax.
